chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Aban from Isa al-Qummi from Amr ibn Hurayth said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mulberry tree; is it sold to be made into a cross or an idol? He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell mulberry trees for making crosses or idols?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *khasbiyyah* (specific intention) in commercial transactions, ruling that a mulberry tree is not sold if the buyer intends to use it specifically for making a cross or an idol. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the buyer's purpose (*niyyah*) determining the permissibility of the sale, ensuring that items are not used for religious purposes distinct from Islam. It reflects the broader juristic concern with preventing the proliferation of idolatrous practices through the supply chain of raw materials.
